purpose: Measure the synthetic heavy-versus-light force mechanism frontier on persistent live-insurgency support rather than default support that can floor-collapse reproductive outcomes.
primary_questions: At each logistics/terrain burden, how much additional insurgent suppression is produced by greater firepower/protection?
At each combat-benefit level, where does the ranking versus the light baseline reverse as supply burden and terrain penalty rise?
Does a heavier profile reduce government losses enough to offset readiness/supply penalties?
How much suppression remains 120 days after the equipment intervention ends?
analysis_guard: Report the benefit-burden response surface and break-even frontier; do not declare one universal armored/light winner. Profiles are stylized force-mechanism analogues, not real vehicle or unit specifications.
cost_guard: The equipment mechanism has operational supply/readiness burden but no empirically calibrated procurement-dollar model. Do not report dollar cost-effectiveness for heavy equipment from this assay.
